title: privacy-scan config
description: Per-repo rules for the shared privacy scanner in amajail/dev-kit. The engine is shared; these rules are not, because what counts as private differs per repo.

rule.description: A pattern plus a human description of what it matches. Array form is [pattern, what]; object form adds `unless`.

pattern.description: JS regex source. Prefix with (?i) for case-insensitive. Lookahead/lookbehind supported — used to exempt a single known-safe value such as the well-known Azurite dev key.

what.description: What this is, in words, e.g. 'a bank statement'. Shown to whoever is blocked.

unless.description: Patterns that re-allow a match, e.g. CSV is a bank export everywhere except under tests/fixtures/.

privatePaths.description: Paths that must never be committed. Deterministic — these deny outright. ADDED to the built-in defaults (.env, local.settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .mcp.json).

secretPatterns.description: Regexes over ADDED lines only, so pre-existing text never re-fails a later PR. ADDED to the built-in credential shapes unless disableDefaultSecrets is set.

disableDefaultSecrets.description: Drop the built-in credential patterns. Rarely correct — prefer adding to them.

fixturePaths.description: Where fake numbers are the whole point, so the private-terms check stays quiet. REPLACES the defaults if given.

safePrefixes.description: Where ordinary work lives. Only affects the broad-`git add` heuristic in hook mode: anything outside these prompts the owner rather than denying.

safeRootFiles.description: Individual non-prefixed paths that are fine to stage, e.g. package.json.

privateTermsFile.description: Path to a gitignored newline-separated list of real terms (tickers, merchant names). A term appearing beside a number outside a fixture prompts the owner. Gitignored on purpose: a committed list of real terms is itself a disclosure — so CI can never run this check.

selfExempt.description: Files exempt from CONTENT rules because they necessarily contain the patterns they look for (this config, the scanner). Never exempt from PATH rules.

refsDir.description: Local-only corpus of real documents for --against-refs. Supports a leading ~. Never available in CI, by design.

benignTokens.description: Regex for tokens that legitimately coincide with real-document text (calendar years, statutory reference numbers). Used by --against-refs only.

wording.description: Domain wording for the messages shown to whoever is blocked.

boundary.description: What .gitignore is protecting, e.g. 'real holdings and credentials'.

placeholders.description: What to use instead, e.g. 'placeholder values (SYMBOL, 123.45)'.

confirm.description: What to check for when asked to confirm a broad add.

fixHint.description: Closing line: where the real thing belongs, and how to fix the rule rather than work around it.
